get.description: Read a project artifact revision including its full source code and version number. Supply revision_id alone to read an exact saved revision, including the preprocessor_artifact_revision_id returned by get_judge. Alternatively, supply artifact_id with version to inspect an exact save, or omit version to return the highest version. Do not combine revision_id with artifact_id or version. Returns null if the revision ID is absent from this project, or if the artifact exists but the requested version does not. Use artifact_id without version to choose the next version; concurrent writers can still conflict on that version.

post.description: Create a project-owned code artifact and its initial immutable Supabase source revision in one call. Supply the name, scope, filename, and complete source code. Returns the artifact and revision metadata without echoing the source. This does not execute code or attach the artifact to a judge. The organization, project, scope, and exact name identify the artifact; its initial revision is version 1. Retrying identical input returns the same records. Different content at version 1 is a conflict; use create_supabase_artifact_revision with a new version for later saves.

filename.description: The source filename, such as preprocess.js

post.description: Store a later immutable source-code revision for an existing artifact in this project. To create a new artifact with its initial source revision, use create_artifact instead. Supply the complete source code; storage and byte size are managed automatically. Returns revision metadata. This does not execute code, change existing revisions, or attach the revision to a judge. Supply a positive integer version and reuse it when retrying the same save. An existing version with identical source and filename is returned unchanged; different content is a conflict. Read get_artifact_revision to inspect an exact version or find the highest version before choosing the next one.

post.description: Backtest unsaved preprocessing source against one historical trace using an exact saved judge version. Runs preprocessing/JEV and an independent ordinary agent judge (AAAJ) in parallel with the same resolved rubric, current judge knowledge, and output definitions. Returns the candidate verdict/confidence or fallback/error diagnostics, the AAAJ verdict/explanation, timing for both paths, evidence size, and matches (null unless the candidate is accepted and AAAJ completes). AAAJ always bypasses optimistic evaluation and runs even when the candidate succeeds or falls back. Consumes both JEV and ordinary-agent evaluation usage and may take longer than the candidate-only 30-second deadline. Does not save artifacts, attach source, change toggles, or persist evaluation score rows. One path failing preserves the other result. Only whole-trace binary/categorical prompt judges in SaaS with BYOK disabled are supported, even when their optimistic toggle is off. Use test_preprocessing_candidate separately to inspect extracted evidence and script diagnostics.

post.description: Test an unsaved preprocessing script against one historical trace using the production sandbox and read-only, trace-scoped SQL. The script receives { traceId, sql }; sql.query(text) returns virtual SQL rows. Return JSON evidence and validate extraction assumptions by throwing on unsupported or incomplete input. No imports, network, model calls, or writes are available. Returns complete evidence up to 50 KiB, its UTF-8 JSON size, sandbox timing, or bounded failure diagnostics. The limit covers evidence alone; production also counts the rubric. This does not save artifacts, change judge configuration, run JEV or AAAJ, or establish verdict accuracy. Use Code Mode to inspect selected evidence fields instead of printing large results.
